61	- F-64 **The compiled checker refuses every type that an api declares, trait or object, that extends a trait whose `comprises` clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not (row 354, open).** So the form `comprises { T, ... }` cannot stand in an api that declares `T`. The refusal runs only when the checker checks an api, so a component's types may extend such a trait. The specification's text allows `...` in an api's clause, and an extender that the clause lists (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). Only a draft note refuses the api's own declaration of an extender, and a release build leaves draft notes out. The team's `compiler_tests/XXX3q` and `XXX10p` pin the refusal, so a fix that skips it for a listed type turns them red. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/REPORT.md`, "Defects and their homes".
62	- F-65 **The checker memoizes `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` per trait table, and the memo changes no answer.** `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false` turns it off. By reading, both functions depend only on the table and the type. One differential on climb batch 7C's tree gave the same errors at the same sites with the memo off and on: 626 at the distance stage and 75 at the count stage. With the memo off, the count stage's 900-second limit stopped it; a copy with the limit raised took 1,149 s, against 112 s with the memo on. F-240 gives the stage's time today, with the memo on; its time with the memo off has not been measured since. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/REPORT.md`, "Why the memo changes no answer"; `reviews/row-488-probe.md`, "The answer".
63	- F-66 **The checker-count stage's table, `gate/checker-count.txt`, lands with every batch beside the gate's `summary.txt`.** Its total at the last landed gate is F-53's count. Step 8 of a batch's gate compares it with the newest landed table. The total is never red on its own, as P-39 rules, since a fix can raise it and the effects of two rungs on it do not add up. The gate is red on a crash line that no rung declared in its manifest (`expectedCheckerCrash`), on a table with no total, and on a stale shadow: the instrumented copy of `StaticChecker` beside the stage (`checker-count/shadow-src/`), when the tracked `StaticChecker` no longer matches the checksum that `run.sh` records. Detail: `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage".
64	- F-67 **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters.** A size is a size parameter's name, a literal or an operation on sizes. Two sizes are equal when their written forms are, once each operation on numerals is computed, so `2 3` equals `6` but `m n` does not equal `n m` (F-146). The checker refuses to infer a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static argument (`XXXNatBoolChecker`). It does not compare `bool` arguments, so `object F extends { Flag[\true\], Flag[\false\] }`, two instantiations of one trait, passes it, and code generation then stops on it (row 406, open, a part of P-40 still to build). A call that leaves a size unknown is refused, "Could not infer static argument ... without context"; F-69 gives when an overload set is refused and when it is not. It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`, `NatExportChecker` and `XXXNatMismatchChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 1.
65	- F-68 **The checker's return-type rule reads a size as it reads a type parameter.** A size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved stays that declaration's own parameter, as `Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick` binds `Δ2`. So an override returning `Dn[\T,3,s\]` over `Up[\T,b,s\]` is refused, like its type-parameter twin, and the library's `subarray` override passes. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOverrideChecker` and `XXXNatRetSizeChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 5.
66	- F-69 **The compiled checker refuses a call whose most specific arm failed only on a size that the call cannot fix, when that arm's parameter types are free of the size.** The message is "Could not infer static argument nat n without context". It drops instead an arm whose unknown size is in its own parameter types (row 400, open). It lets through a call whose argument's static type lies above the arm's domain, and the compiled run dies reading the size (row 446, open). It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatKnownSizeArm`, which compiles and runs a call that fixes the size, and `XXXNatUnknownSize*`, which pin the refusal's message; rows 400 and 446 have no test. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-unknown-size-arm/REPORT.md` section 10.
67	- F-70 **The compiled checker checks a static argument written at a dotted method call against its parameter's bound, but not one written at a top-level function call.** At a dotted call it puts the written arguments into each bound and refuses a call whose argument misses one, "No such method" (row 651, fixed). At a top-level call it matches kinds only, so `n[\String\]("d")` passes for `n[\T extends Number\](s: String): T` (row 470, open). Gated by `compiler_tests/MethodStaticArgsBoundNamesOther*`, which accept a dotted call whose written arguments meet their bounds. No test pins the refusal of an argument that misses its bound; a probe showed it (`rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 6). Row 470 can have no gated test, since the harness has no form for a program that the specification refuses and the checker accepts. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
68	- F-71 **The compiled checker does not narrow the variable of the shorthand form `typecase x of T => ...`, neither path accepts the binding form `typecase x = e of`, and the clause-binding form `typecase e of y: T => ... end` runs on both paths.** So write the clause-binding form, as the library does (F-134): its `cast` writes `typecase x of x':T => x' ... end`. In the shorthand form, the checker refuses a clause that uses `x` as a `T`, and such a clause runs under walk only; a clause that does not, as in the library's `instanceOf`, passes. The binding form parses as the equality `x = e`. Only the specification's grammar has it, under the team's note that the section awaits the pattern-matching proposal (`typecase.tex:15`). Row 460 records both refusals, and no test gates them. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/REPORT.md` section 15.
69	- F-72 **The compiled checker reads a `comprises` clause for a generic subtrait as the team's 2012 texts do (Luchangco's Types chapter and Welterweight; P-44): the subtrait may extend the closed trait when the trait table knows at least one type that immediately extends the subtrait, and each such type is below a listed type.** It builds P-44. This rule leaves the ellipsis refusal of F-64 (row 354, open) as it was. Open: an extender in another compilation unit escapes the check, the hole that P-44 leaves (row 487). The verdict changes when the extender renames its type variable (row 489), and the extenders are found by the simple text of the trait's name (row 490). Gated by `compiler_tests/ComprisesGenericSubtrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/REPORT.md` section 6.
70	- F-73 **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion: a type parameter that is the whole type of each parameter it occurs in, as `T` in `pick[\T\](x: T, y: T)`, takes the narrowest type that every one of its arguments converts into and its bound permits.** It looks for that type among its arguments' types, their coercion targets and its bound, the bound only when it is a trait type other than `Object` or `Any`. It builds P-74 and P-49. A coerced declaration ranks below one that needs no coercion. A tie among coerced declarations is refused, "Ambiguous coercion", outside three narrow cases (the report's section 3.2). When the tied declarations differ only at positions where the call passes a numeral, the checker reads the numeral as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit; that reading is a default. The coercion attempt refuses a call beyond 64 combinations of candidate types (row 506) and a call with an untyped function argument (row 507). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatLitArgChecker`, `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC` and `InferCoercionShapes`, which F-51 also cites, and the refusal of a tie by `XXXInferAmbiguousCoercion`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2.
71	- F-74 **Under walk, an integer numeral takes its type from its value: a `ZZ32` if it fits 32 bits, a `ZZ64` if it fits 64 bits, a `ZZ` above that; it stays so until walk has the checker's static types, since without them a list of numerals and a generic's static argument take their types from the values.** Its run-time type is the library's value object `Int`, `Long` or `BigNum`, below `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:125`, `:128`, `:223`). Walk instantiates a generic at it, so a `Box[\Int\]` is a type apart from `Box[\ZZ32\]` and dispatches past it (row 364). F-74 is why P-76's walk half waits; F-79 is the library half, built. Probe Q (`compile-ladder/plan-n/probe-q/PROBE-Q.md`) measured walk with every integer numeral an `IntLiteral`, the numeral's own type in the library. It ran before climb batch N's second run and before the library half landed. Alone, the switch changed 59 test verdicts. With four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter read as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, a varargs list converted at dispatch), the library loaded and both microGPT checks kept their values, but 24 passing interpreter tests failed: 6 by design, 3 of them team tests that assert a `ZZ32`; 9 for want of static types (rows 364, 510); and 9 walk gaps. A size used as a value is a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and a `ZZ64` above (row 486; F-140). Detail: `reviews/numeral-switch-judgement.md` sections 2 and 3.
72	- F-75 **The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and a positional rule: when two generic declarations in the more-specific relation declare as many static parameters of their own, those parameters agree in kind by position, and the more specific return type is a subtype of the other once the other's parameters are read as its own by position.** The equal-count scope and the comparison of kinds are the rung's choices. It builds P-45. Checking every instance, as P-45 asks, it also refuses a generic declaration beside a plain one whose domain is an object type, a pair that the type group's 2011 paper (`Papers/Types/`) accepts, since the paper sets aside the instances whose domains cannot meet (row 542, open). In the interpreter's library the two rules refuse no pair: the distance holds no return-type or overloading error (F-53). Gated by `compiler_tests/OverloadGeneric*` and `OverloadBoundNamesForced`, which accept; `XXXOverloadReturnEveryInstance` and `XXXOverloadPermutedStaticParams`, which pin the two rules' refusals; and `XXXOverloadReturnObjectDomain`, which pins row 542's. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 1 and 2.
73	- F-76 **The compiled checker accepts the specification's `comprises` example of the Meet Rule (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, "The Meet Rule for Functions") by a coverage check used only in overload checking, not in its subtype test, and types a call whose argument's static type lies below closed traits and above the types that they list by the intersection of the return types of its most specific declarations, when they tie without coercion.** It builds P-60, which reads `comprises` at the level of values: several declarations below two overloads serve as their meet if together they cover it. Open: coverage refuses a pair when a declaration that it compares has static parameters (row 546). In an accepted family that has any other generic declaration, such a call is typed by the head of a sort, which follows declaration order and can vary between runs, not by the intersection (row 543). That narrower scope than P-60's is a default. On the compiled path, a method call on a value typed by the intersection crashes the code generator (row 540), and a generic declaration instantiated at an intersection type dies as it loads (row 559). The checker checks a `comprises` clause only at the closed trait's immediate subtypes, so a type in another component below a generic subtrait escapes it (row 487). Its verdict on an overload set can depend on the components compiled before it in the same JVM (row 547). Gated by `compiler_tests/*Comprises*` and `*CoverageReturn*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 3 and 4.
74	- F-77 **The one library repairs its refused overload families with its own exclusions, and the checker accepts its `seq` pairs by the rule for functional methods (F-80).** It builds P-45. `StandardMin`, `StandardMax`, `SequentialGenerator` and `FilterGenerator` exclude `HasRank`, `String` excludes `AnyMultiplicativeRing`, and `TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax` (P-98). Marker traits instead would give two ordered types several minimal common supertypes, which walk mishandles (rows 555, 589). Gated by `tests/LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overload-families/REPORT.md` section 4.
75	- F-78 **The compiled checker instantiates a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes at the intersection of its upper bounds, never `BottomType`, and tries a call by subtyping without the expected type first.** It builds P-48 and P-49. Where the call has an expected type, its attempts come in this order: subtyping without the expected type, kept when its result converts to it; subtyping with the expected type; coercion with it; and coercion without it. The second lets a call whose untyped function argument only the expected type fixes type-check, since the coercion attempt cannot check such an argument (row 507). P-49 decides the first and the third; the second and the fourth are an agent's choice, the instance-bound rung's (its decision record, D4). An argument of intersection type fixes a parameter at the whole intersection, not at one conjunct (row 541). The run time has no class for an intersection type, so such an instance dies as it loads (row 559). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferResultOnly*` and `InferContextKeepsFit`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 7; the order, by reading, `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md`, D4, and `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:733-737`.
76	- F-79 **In the interpreter's library, `IntLiteral`, the type that the compiled checker gives an integer numeral, is declared on the model of the compiler's prelude: a sibling of the number types under `Number`, which each integer type, `QQ`, `RR64` and `AnyIntegral` convert from by coercion.** It builds the library half of P-76. Under walk a numeral is still a `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, so no numeral reaches these declarations until walk's half is built (F-74). `IntLiteral` declares itself the members of `Integral[\I\]` that a numeral could not reach, among them the getters `zero` and `one`, `odd`, `even`, `floor` and `DIVIDES`. There are three reasons: for some, no declaration of `Integral` applies to a sibling type even with coercion; for others, the declarations that apply by coercion tie; and a getter must be the type's own member. Each integer type declares its own comparisons, `CMP`, `MAXNUM` and `MINNUM`, and a `^` with an `IntLiteral` exponent. Without them, a typed integer with a numeral operand ties between a declaration inherited from a generic trait and the same operator's own declarations in `ZZ64`, `QQ` and `RR64`. The compiled checker refuses `(3).minimum` and `(3).maximum`, `ZZ32`'s getters (row 581). Gated under walk by `tests/IntegerOrderNumerals.fss`, which checks each integer type's own comparisons, `MAXNUM` and `MINNUM`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-numeral-library/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 6.
77	- F-80 **The compiled checker judges two functional methods of one name, abstract declarations included, by the Meet Rule for Functional Methods in each type that provides both.** Such a type must provide their meet, compared without the `self` parameter. F-88 says what a type provides. An abstract functional method beside a concrete one in the same trait, with the same parameter types, is refused by the No Duplicates Rule. Unchecked: a pair that only an object expression provides (row 570). It checks every operator, a symbol such as `+`, `<`, `||` or a subscript as well as a name of capitals such as `CAP` or a word such as `juxtaposition` (F-281). The checker's overloading memo is keyed on all the inputs of the check, so a pair accepted at the top level is not reused unchecked in a trait that provides it. Gated by `compiler_tests/FunctionalMethodMeet*`, and by the refusals that the specification asks for, `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetAbstractSibling`, `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract` and, for an operator, `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperatorChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 7; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-abstract-callsite/REPORT.md` section 1.
78	- F-81 **In the interpreter's library, every Meet Rule pair inside one type that the compiled checker checks has a declaration on its meet, and the checker checks every operator (F-281).** `String`'s juxtaposition is three top-level operators, since two functional methods with `self` at different positions have no meet. `String`'s `||`, `|||`, `//` and `///`, which paired `(a:Any, self)` with `(self, b:Any)`, the shape the specification refuses, are now three top-level operators each too (F-276). F-245's measurement found other invalid pairs, among them `Indexed`'s three subscripts in 17 types, valid since the index bound (F-278). The rung that added these meets also set the declared types listed in report section 1 to what their bodies answer. `__bigOperator2`'s fused branch, whose arm's type the `typecase` cannot show, casts its result to the declared `O0` (F-85). Gated by `tests/LibraryMeetDeclarations.fss`, and for the symbolic operators by the distance stage, which finds no overloading error in the library (F-245). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-meets/REPORT.md` section 1.
79	- F-82 **In the interpreter's library, the range types declare a method on the meet for each of their Meet Rule pairs that the compiled checker checks, and their declared types match what their bodies answer.** Among the meets are `CAP` at each rank, a range's number of dimensions (F-89 holds the ranks' kinds), and `FullRange`'s abstract `IN`, so a numeral `IN` a `#` or `:` range type-checks (row 580, fixed). The pairs of `Indexed`'s three subscripts have no meet in the ranges and need none since the index bound (F-278). Open library bug (row 603): the full sequential ranges' `map` answers a `SimpleMappedSeqIndexed`, which is no `MappedGenerator`, so its `reverse` is `Indexed`'s. The elements and their order are right, but the string differs: `seq(0:6:2).map(fn x => x + 1).reverse.asString` prints `SimpleReversedIndexed(mapped(seq(1,3,5,7)))`, not `mapped(7,5,3,1)`. `tests/RangeDeclarations.fss` pins that string, and gates the meets. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-range-meets/REPORT.md` section 1.
80	- F-83 **In the interpreter's library, the string components `String.fss` and `FlatString.fss` hold no site of the distance, the compiled checker's errors in that library (F-53), and the rung's repairs of their refused declarations are in forms that the library already uses.** The trait `String` is declared in `FortressLibrary`, not in `String.fss`, which holds string objects and traits such as `CatString` and `SubString`. `String`'s api writes `abstract` on the members its component's trait leaves without a body or does not declare, and its `excludes` clause is the component's (F-286), so `String` has no entry in the `FortressLibrary` export error. `FlatString`'s api declares its component's header, `extends { String, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\] }`, and no `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)` (F-259). Open library bugs: `FlatString.rangeContains` finds only the first occurrence of the character, and so does `CatString`'s, through its flat halves (row 607). An implicit strided subscript `[:b:c]` is completed from the axis's right end, not from its left as `l:b:c`: `"abcdef"[:3:2]` is `bd`, not `ac` (row 609; the expected failure `tests/XXXSubscriptImplicitStridedRange.fss` holds the specification's answer). Gated by `tests/StringPieces.fss`, which pins row 607's two wrong `false` answers. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-string-slips/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 8.
81	- F-84 **In the interpreter's library, the result-only type parameters of `fail`, `builtinPrimitive` and `List`'s comprehension operator `BIG <|[\T\]|>` are unbounded, as the team declared them, and the same rung repaired 25 of the compiled checker's 60 one-off error sites in numbers, orderings, `List` and natives, each by a declared type, a body or an api header, in forms that the library already uses.** A result-only parameter occurs only in the result type. P-48 gives it the intersection of its upper bounds, narrowed by the expected type, so where `()` is expected its instance is `()`. The rung also made `MatchFailure` an unchecked exception: it extends `UncheckedException` (row 590). The sites that it left have rows (report section 5). Limit: under walk the name `IntLiteral` also denotes a value, a zero that no numeral reaches, and its arithmetic answers a `ZZ32` against its declared `IntLiteral` (row 578). F-263 holds the integer powers' types, and F-255 `List`'s ordering. The compiler's prelude has instead `fail(s: String): Zilch` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:33`), a declared bottom result that Steele put in place of the generic `fail` in `0886e9654` (2011-06-13), and it does not bind the one library, since the team's later word makes `Bottom` inexpressible in a program (the 2012 Types chapter; POPL 2019, `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019.txt:437-438`) and binds an unfixed parameter by its bounds and the expected type, P-48's rule; walk cannot evaluate `Zilch`. Gated under walk by `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-number-order-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1, 4 and 5.
82	- F-85 **In the interpreter's library, the rung's repairs of the generator, condition, reduction and nested-generator declarations that the compiled checker refused are in forms that the library already uses. `__bigOperator2`'s fused branch passes its result through `cast[\O0\]`.** That branch, the `typecase` branch that runs a nested big operator through `generate2`, casts its result to `O0` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1476`), the library's device for an arm whose type the `typecase` cannot show (F-264), so the checker no longer types its body `OR(I0,O0)` where `O0` is declared (row 632) and no site of these declarations is on the distance (F-53). Each method body of `Condition` that calls `cond` writes the call's result type as its static argument, such as `cond[\Maybe[\G\]\]`. The sites that the rung left were cleared by other work: F-250 holds the identity functions' `cast` and the typed `embiggen`, F-93 how library code reads a generator's size and index (row 629), and F-144 how the reductions without an identity are typed at their element type (row 628). Gated by `tests/GeneratorDeclarations.fss` and `tests/NestedReductionFusion.fss`, which run the arm fused, and the cast by the distance stage. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generator-slips/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 8; `compile-ladder/rung-body-arguments/REPORT.md` section 9.
83	- F-86 **The compiled checker types a varargs parameter as the team's `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]`, and applies a varargs declaration by the specification's expansion rule.** The rule reads such a declaration as one declaration for each number of arguments that it can take (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex`, "Applicability for Functionals with Varargs and Keyword Parameters"). Over the interpreter's library, a body uses the parameter as that array. The compiled library declares no `ImmutableArray`, so under it each use of such a parameter is refused (row 604). The code generator refuses varargs (row 624). Gated by `compiler_tests/Varargs*`, and the refusals by the `XXXVarargs*` tests of rows 604 and 624. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-defects/REPORT.md` section 4.
84	- F-87 **Besides the contexts that it already had, such as a typed declaration's right-hand side, the compiled checker gives a call its expected type in a clause of an `if` without `else` (the type `()`), a block's last expression after local declarations, a `typecase` clause, a juxtaposition, an operator repeated between three or more operands, a `label` body and each value that an `exit` gives the `label`, and, by a retry of the enclosing call, another call's argument.** The inference chapter lists every context (`Specification/basic/inference.tex`, "The Static Arguments of a Call", "The expected type"). In a juxtaposition or a repeated operator, the expression's own expected type goes to the application that it makes. The `label` contexts build P-50. At another call's argument, it retries the enclosing call against each declaration's parameter type, as P-51 decides (F-221). F-226 gives how it renames an inherited method's static parameters at a call, and F-70 where it checks a written static argument against its bound. Gated by `compiler_tests/InferResultOnly*`, among them `InferResultOnlyLabelBody`, a type-check test, since the code generator has no `label`, and `Infer*Context`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
85	- F-88 **The compiled checker reads what a trait or object provides by the traits chapter's inheritance, and checks an overriding declaration's return type against the one it overrides.** A type provides its own methods and its immediate supertypes', less those that an own declaration overrides or repeats in its parameter types. So an object below a trait that redeclares an inherited method abstract must define it. The code generator refuses `override` (row 650). Gated by `compiler_tests/Override*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-overloading/REPORT.md` section 1.
86	- F-89 **The one library's ranges of rank 2 and 3 have bounded kinds, their comparisons are declared at the `ZZ32` kinds, and `#(0,n)` is empty.** `BoundedRange2D` and `BoundedRange3D` are the meets of `Range2D` or `Range3D` and `BoundedRange`, and the left, right and full kinds extend them. The generic range traits declare `CMP`, `FORWARD_CMP` and the compact kinds' size abstract, and the `ZZ32` kinds of rank 1 to 3 define them. `#0`, `#(0,n)` and `#(0,n,m)` are empty: `|#(0,3)|` is 0. Gated by `tests/RangeKindBodies.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-range-types/REPORT.md` section 1.
87	- F-90 **In the interpreter's library, several array and matrix declarations and `SUFFIX_SUM` are written so that the compiled checker accepts them: `__DefaultVector`, `__DefaultMatrix` and `TransposedMatrix` declare the array family's bound `T extends { Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }`, which F-151 owns; `__immutableFactory1` is declared to answer an `ImmutableArray1` (its branch for lowest index 0 is cast to that type, F-264); `__ImmutableSubArray1` has no `put`; `Matrix`'s `mul` writes its two parallel calls, once a tuple typed `((), ())`, as a parallel `do … also do … end` block, typed `()`; and `TransposedMatrix`'s `add`, `subtract` and `negate` call `Matrix`'s operators.** The unary operator `SUFFIX_SUM` on a `ZZ32` array (`FortressLibrary.fsi`) loops over `seq((0 # (|x| - 1)).reverse)`, since a strided range `a:b:c` is declared `Range[\ZZ32\]`, which is no generator, so the checker refuses `seq(a:b:c)` (row 661, open). - F-64 **The compiled checker refuses every type that an api declares, trait or object, that extends a trait whose `comprises` clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not (row 354, open).** So the form `comprises { T, ... }` cannot stand in an api that declares `T`. The refusal runs only when the checker checks an api, so a component's types may extend such a trait. The specification's text allows `...` in an api's clause, and an extender that the clause lists (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). Only a draft note refuses the api's own declaration of an extender, and a release build leaves draft notes out. The team's `compiler_tests/XXX3q` and `XXX10p` pin the refusal, so a fix that skips it for a listed type turns them red. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/REPORT.md`, "Defects and their homes".
- F-65 **The checker memoizes `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` per trait table, and the memo changes no answer.** `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false` turns it off. By reading, both functions depend only on the table and the type. One differential on climb batch 7C's tree gave the same errors at the same sites with the memo off and on: 626 at the distance stage and 75 at the count stage. With the memo off, the count stage's 900-second limit stopped it; a copy with the limit raised took 1,149 s, against 112 s with the memo on. F-240 gives the stage's time today, with the memo on; its time with the memo off has not been measured since. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/REPORT.md`, "Why the memo changes no answer"; `reviews/row-488-probe.md`, "The answer".
- F-66 **The checker-count stage's table, `gate/checker-count.txt`, lands with every batch beside the gate's `summary.txt`.** Its total at the last landed gate is F-53's count. Step 8 of a batch's gate compares it with the newest landed table. The total is never red on its own, as P-39 rules, since a fix can raise it and the effects of two rungs on it do not add up. The gate is red on a crash line that no rung declared in its manifest (`expectedCheckerCrash`), on a table with no total, and on a stale shadow: the instrumented copy of `StaticChecker` beside the stage (`checker-count/shadow-src/`), when the tracked `StaticChecker` no longer matches the checksum that `run.sh` records. Detail: `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage".
- F-67 **The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters.** A size is a size parameter's name, a literal or an operation on sizes. Two sizes are equal when their written forms are, once each operation on numerals is computed, so `2 3` equals `6` but `m n` does not equal `n m` (F-146). The checker refuses to infer a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static argument (`XXXNatBoolChecker`). It does not compare `bool` arguments, so `object F extends { Flag[\true\], Flag[\false\] }`, two instantiations of one trait, passes it, and code generation then stops on it (row 406, open, a part of P-40 still to build). A call that leaves a size unknown is refused, "Could not infer static argument ... without context"; F-69 gives when an overload set is refused and when it is not. It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`, `NatExportChecker` and `XXXNatMismatchChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-68 **The checker's return-type rule reads a size as it reads a type parameter.** A size of the less specific declaration that the domains leave unsolved stays that declaration's own parameter, as `Papers/Types/overloading-check.tick` binds `Δ2`. So an override returning `Dn[\T,3,s\]` over `Up[\T,b,s\]` is refused, like its type-parameter twin, and the library's `subarray` override passes. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOverrideChecker` and `XXXNatRetSizeChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-69 **The compiled checker refuses a call whose most specific arm failed only on a size that the call cannot fix, when that arm's parameter types are free of the size.** The message is "Could not infer static argument nat n without context". It drops instead an arm whose unknown size is in its own parameter types (row 400, open). It lets through a call whose argument's static type lies above the arm's domain, and the compiled run dies reading the size (row 446, open). It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatKnownSizeArm`, which compiles and runs a call that fixes the size, and `XXXNatUnknownSize*`, which pin the refusal's message; rows 400 and 446 have no test. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-unknown-size-arm/REPORT.md` section 10.
- F-70 **The compiled checker checks a static argument written at a dotted method call against its parameter's bound, but not one written at a top-level function call.** At a dotted call it puts the written arguments into each bound and refuses a call whose argument misses one, "No such method" (row 651, fixed). At a top-level call it matches kinds only, so `n[\String\]("d")` passes for `n[\T extends Number\](s: String): T` (row 470, open). Gated by `compiler_tests/MethodStaticArgsBoundNamesOther*`, which accept a dotted call whose written arguments meet their bounds. No test pins the refusal of an argument that misses its bound; a probe showed it (`rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 6). Row 470 can have no gated test, since the harness has no form for a program that the specification refuses and the checker accepts. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-71 **The compiled checker does not narrow the variable of the shorthand form `typecase x of T => ...`, neither path accepts the binding form `typecase x = e of`, and the clause-binding form `typecase e of y: T => ... end` runs on both paths.** So write the clause-binding form, as the library does (F-134): its `cast` writes `typecase x of x':T => x' ... end`. In the shorthand form, the checker refuses a clause that uses `x` as a `T`, and such a clause runs under walk only; a clause that does not, as in the library's `instanceOf`, passes. The binding form parses as the equality `x = e`. Only the specification's grammar has it, under the team's note that the section awaits the pattern-matching proposal (`typecase.tex:15`). Row 460 records both refusals, and no test gates them. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-exclusion-remainder/REPORT.md` section 15.
- F-72 **The compiled checker reads a `comprises` clause for a generic subtrait as the team's 2012 texts do (Luchangco's Types chapter and Welterweight; P-44): the subtrait may extend the closed trait when the trait table knows at least one type that immediately extends the subtrait, and each such type is below a listed type.** It builds P-44. This rule leaves the ellipsis refusal of F-64 (row 354, open) as it was. Open: an extender in another compilation unit escapes the check, the hole that P-44 leaves (row 487). The verdict changes when the extender renames its type variable (row 489), and the extenders are found by the simple text of the trait's name (row 490). Gated by `compiler_tests/ComprisesGenericSubtrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/REPORT.md` section 6.
- F-73 **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion: a type parameter that is the whole type of each parameter it occurs in, as `T` in `pick[\T\](x: T, y: T)`, takes the narrowest type that every one of its arguments converts into and its bound permits.** It looks for that type among its arguments' types, their coercion targets and its bound, the bound only when it is a trait type other than `Object` or `Any`. It builds P-74 and P-49. A coerced declaration ranks below one that needs no coercion. A tie among coerced declarations is refused, "Ambiguous coercion", outside three narrow cases (the report's section 3.2). When the tied declarations differ only at positions where the call passes a numeral, the checker reads the numeral as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit; that reading is a default. The coercion attempt refuses a call beyond 64 combinations of candidate types (row 506) and a call with an untyped function argument (row 507). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatLitArgChecker`, `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC` and `InferCoercionShapes`, which F-51 also cites, and the refusal of a tie by `XXXInferAmbiguousCoercion`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2.
- F-74 **Under walk, an integer numeral takes its type from its value: a `ZZ32` if it fits 32 bits, a `ZZ64` if it fits 64 bits, a `ZZ` above that; it stays so until walk has the checker's static types, since without them a list of numerals and a generic's static argument take their types from the values.** Its run-time type is the library's value object `Int`, `Long` or `BigNum`, below `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:125`, `:128`, `:223`). Walk instantiates a generic at it, so a `Box[\Int\]` is a type apart from `Box[\ZZ32\]` and dispatches past it (row 364). F-74 is why P-76's walk half waits; F-79 is the library half, built. Probe Q (`compile-ladder/plan-n/probe-q/PROBE-Q.md`) measured walk with every integer numeral an `IntLiteral`, the numeral's own type in the library. With four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter read as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, a varargs list converted at dispatch), the library loaded and both microGPT checks kept their values, but 24 passing interpreter tests failed: 6 by design, 3 of them team tests that assert a `ZZ32`; 9 for want of static types (rows 364, 510); and 9 walk gaps. A size used as a value is a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and a `ZZ64` above (row 486; F-140). Detail: `reviews/numeral-switch-judgement.md` sections 2 and 3.
- F-75 **The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and a positional rule: when two generic declarations in the more-specific relation declare as many static parameters of their own, those parameters agree in kind by position, and the more specific return type is a subtype of the other once the other's parameters are read as its own by position.** The equal-count scope and the comparison of kinds are the rung's choices. It builds P-45. Checking every instance, as P-45 asks, it also refuses a generic declaration beside a plain one whose domain is an object type, a pair that the type group's 2011 paper (`Papers/Types/`) accepts, since the paper sets aside the instances whose domains cannot meet (row 542, open). In the interpreter's library the two rules refuse no pair: the distance holds no return-type or overloading error (F-53). Gated by `compiler_tests/OverloadGeneric*` and `OverloadBoundNamesForced`, which accept; `XXXOverloadReturnEveryInstance` and `XXXOverloadPermutedStaticParams`, which pin the two rules' refusals; and `XXXOverloadReturnObjectDomain`, which pins row 542's. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 1 and 2.
- F-76 **The compiled checker accepts the specification's `comprises` example of the Meet Rule (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, "The Meet Rule for Functions") by a coverage check used only in overload checking, not in its subtype test, and types a call whose argument's static type lies below closed traits and above the types that they list by the intersection of the return types of its most specific declarations, when they tie without coercion.** It builds P-60, which reads `comprises` at the level of values: several declarations below two overloads serve as their meet if together they cover it. Open: coverage refuses a pair when a declaration that it compares has static parameters (row 546). In an accepted family that has any other generic declaration, such a call is typed by the head of a sort, which follows declaration order and can vary between runs, not by the intersection (row 543). That narrower scope than P-60's is a default. On the compiled path, a method call on a value typed by the intersection crashes the code generator (row 540), and a generic declaration instantiated at an intersection type dies as it loads (row 559). The checker checks a `comprises` clause only at the closed trait's immediate subtypes, so a type in another component below a generic subtrait escapes it (row 487). Its verdict on an overload set can depend on the components compiled before it in the same JVM (row 547). Gated by `compiler_tests/*Comprises*` and `*CoverageReturn*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-77 **The one library repairs its refused overload families with its own exclusions, and the checker accepts its `seq` pairs by the rule for functional methods (F-80).** It builds P-45. `StandardMin`, `StandardMax`, `SequentialGenerator` and `FilterGenerator` exclude `HasRank`, `String` excludes `AnyMultiplicativeRing`, and `TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax` (P-98). Marker traits instead would give two ordered types several minimal common supertypes, which walk mishandles (rows 555, 589). Gated by `tests/LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss`. - F-78 **The compiled checker instantiates a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes at the intersection of its upper bounds, never `BottomType`, and tries a call by subtyping without the expected type first.** It builds P-48 and P-49. The second lets a call whose untyped function argument only the expected type fixes type-check, since the coercion attempt cannot check such an argument (row 507). P-49 decides the first and the third; the second and the fourth are an agent's choice, the instance-bound rung's (its decision record, D4). An argument of intersection type fixes a parameter at the whole intersection, not at one conjunct (row 541). The run time has no class for an intersection type, so such an instance dies as it loads (row 559). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferResultOnly*` and `InferContextKeepsFit`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 7; the order, by reading, `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md`, D4, and `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:733-737`.
- F-79 **In the interpreter's library, `IntLiteral`, the type that the compiled checker gives an integer numeral, is declared on the model of the compiler's prelude: a sibling of the number types under `Number`, which each integer type, `QQ`, `RR64` and `AnyIntegral` convert from by coercion.** It builds the library half of P-76. There are three reasons: for some, no declaration of `Integral` applies to a sibling type even with coercion; for others, the declarations that apply by coercion tie; and a getter must be the type's own member. F-263 holds the integer powers' types, and F-255 `List`'s ordering. The compiler's prelude has instead `fail(s: String): Zilch` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:33`), a declared bottom result that Steele put in place of the generic `fail` in `0886e9654` (2011-06-13), and it does not bind the one library, since the team's later word makes `Bottom` inexpressible in a program (the 2012 Types chapter; POPL 2019, `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019.txt:437-438`) and binds an unfixed parameter by its bounds and the expected type, P-48's rule; walk cannot evaluate `Zilch`. 216	- F-252 **Under walk, where the parameter-by-parameter check refuses two declarations with static parameters of their own, or one beside a generic trait's functional method that declares none of its own, the load check reads the pair again on its declared domains, by the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules.** A declaration with static parameters of its own is a generic function, a generic object's constructor, or a functional method that declares static parameters in a trait or object that has none. It reads two generic functions of one name and one list of static parameters at one shared symbolic instantiation, and two instances of one generic object as two object types that cannot be extended, so they exclude. A pair whose domains exclude when read whole also loads, where neither declaration has a `where` clause of its own (F-258; row 787). A pair with a varargs parameter is not read again and keeps the parameter check's refusal (F-257). At a call, walk compares a functional method of a generic trait or object on the instance that the call makes. F-253 gives the case of a generic dotted method, where one of the two declared domains can lie inside the other. Gated by `tests/DispatchRenamedGenericArmWalk`, `DispatchSwappedGenericArmWalk` and `GenericPairNestedBoundsWalk` (load and dispatch), and the expected failure `XXXOverloadExistentialMeetWalk` (row 539); for the withdrawal, as refusals at load, by `GenericBoundsNoMeetWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk` and `GenericOverloadInstancesApartWalk`, and as programs that load, by `GenericBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericFBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericPairExcludingWalk`, `GenericSizePairNestedWalk`, `ShuffleTest` and `GenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk`. 218	- F-257 **Under walk, a pair of declarations that the load check refuses after it reads the pair on its declared domains is refused in the name of the rule that the pair breaks.** The load check reads a pair on its declared domains where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses the pair and both declarations have static parameters of their own, or one has them and the other is a plain declaration or a generic trait's functional method that declares none of its own (F-252, F-27, F-318). 219	- F-258 **Walk and the compiled checker read exclusion between two declarations, one or both with static parameters, over the whole parameter type, by existential reduction.** A value of both declared domains has, at each position, one instance of each generic type that the two parameter types there are or extend, so those instances' static arguments are equal; the two domains exclude where these equalities cannot hold together, or where, at the instance they force, the parameter types at some position exclude. The two paths differ on two type parameters whose bounds exclude (row 786); on such a pair one of whose declarations has a `where` clause, which walk refuses and the checker accepts (row 787); and on a pair that walk's parameter check reads apart, reading an object type over a static parameter as excluding a type it is at some instance, as `g[\T\](x: Box[\T\], y: ZZ32)` beside `g(x: Box[\ZZ32\], y: Any)`, which walk loads and the checker refuses (row 788). 220	- F-259 **An object or trait whose `extends` clause names `Any` alone is an `Object` on both paths, but the library's `Index` (F-278), and such an object expression under walk, and `String`'s two top-level `||` over `Any` convert by the library's own way.** The pre-disambiguation desugaring that both paths run gives such a clause `{Object}`, as it gives an empty one, and leaves `Any`'s, `Object`'s and the library's `Index`'s own declarations as written; a clause that names only `Index` (and `Any`) gets `Object` beside it. `opr ||(a:Any, b:String)` is `("" || a) || b` and `opr ||(a:String, b:Any)` is `a || cast[\Object\](b).asString` (top-level since F-276); `FlatString`'s api states its component's header, with no `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-string-conversion/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 4 and 5.
221	- F-261 **Under walk, `unsigned` reinterprets the bits, so a negative exponent converted for an unsigned power overflows at run time.** `unsigned(-1)` is `4294967295`, and `2^unsigned(-1)` raises `IntegerOverflow`, not a sign error. No test checks it. Detail: `reviews/integer-power-fable-judgement.md` sections 8 and 9.
222	- F-262 **A numeral's sign does not reach its type on either path, so no overload on a numeral exponent's type can tell `10^16` from `10^(-16)`.** The numeral itself has no sign (`Specification/basic/lexical-structure.tex:1053-1080`). 223	- F-263 **In the interpreter's library each integer power is declared to answer its base's own type; under walk, at a negative exponent, the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, a base of 0 raises `DivisionByZero`, and any other base raises `IntegerOverflow`.** It builds P-153. Under walk a numeral is a `ZZ32` value (F-74), so `2^(-1)` raises `IntegerOverflow`. `IntLiteral` is the type that the compiled checker gives an integer numeral (F-262). The compiled path's own library does not follow these rules. At a negative exponent its `ZZ32` power gives 0 at every base but 0, 1 and -1, and a raw Java `RuntimeException` at a base of 0 (row 441). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-integer-power/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2 and 4 (the change, the tests, the checker's sites); `perf-probes/integer-power/REPORT.md` section 1.6 (microGPT's powers).
224	- F-270 **The compiled checker opens a value of a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a type at a `where`-clause size: it gives each listed type's `nat` and `int` `where`-clause sizes a fresh name for the call.** In `trait NatParam comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]`, a `NatParam` passed where `N[\$n\]` is expected, `$n` being the checker's inference variable for the called function's size parameter, binds `$n` to the fresh size, and the call's result type carries it. This is way 4a of fork 3 of the array design, a size known only at run time: the checker reads such a size as fixed for that call, not as unknown. P-85 leaves the array design's three questions open with no default; the third stands on this ground, and way 4a is the one way built on it. The code generator compiles such a trait, and a compiled call that opens its value to the size fails the JVM's verification (row 307; `compiler_tests/XXXNatOpenRun`, with `NatOpenRunLink.test`). In row 682's program, with `trait NatParamT comprises { Nt[\n\] } where [\nat n\]`, the checker refuses `f(x: NatParamT)` beside `f[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\])` as two declarations of one parameter type, where walk runs the pair (row 682, contested). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-expressions/REPORT.md` section 1, "Fork 3, way 4a, under Q13.3", and section 12.
225	- F-274 **Under walk, two declarations whose declared domains are equal are refused by the No Duplicates Rule, where one has static parameters of its own and the other has its own or none, whether or not the parameter-by-parameter check orders them.** The parameter check reads a type parameter as strictly below its bound. - F-113 **A harness run against another build's classes must point `FORTRESS_CACHES` at that build's caches as well as passing `-Dfortress.caches`.** A `.test` file's `run` step is a separate `bin/fortress run`, whose class path comes from `FORTRESS_CACHES`. Climb batch 27 ended at 11:57 UTC (12:57 your time), and its push is held for your word.

**Should the hold on climb batch 27's push be lifted?**

- **Why it's held:** rung N's new `=` declarations stopped one team demo, `turnersParaffins0`. That's against your rule that every team demo keeps running. The workflow script holds the push on such a point, and only you can lift it.
- **The repair:** the judge ruled to fix walk and keep the demo as the team wrote it. Walk now calls an overloaded method on a value under `asif` (row 921), and all 52 demos reach their end again. The gate after the repair is green, with the distance at 0 and the checker count at 0.
- **One new thing:** the distance table shows two checker crashes in `FortressBuiltin`, at lines 661 to 773 and in the component's last stage. Climb batch 26's showed none. A crash can hide errors behind the zero. The post-batch review is finding which rung brought them, and whether they bear on the push.

The options:

1. **Lift it now.** I push the eight rungs and the repair, then run the record-landing workflow.
2. **Lift it once the review finds nothing against the push.** I push without asking you again. If the review finds something, I bring it to you first.

Option 1 lands about an hour sooner. Option 2 waits for the review's word on the crashes, and costs you nothing more.

I recommend 2.

What landed, one line each:

- `Number` is open: its `comprises` clause, `asFloat`, `=` and `exactValue` are gone. Each number type declares its own `asFloat` and an `=` for each conversion, 42 in all. The norm is declared at each of the eight types, and the specification is revised.
- The floats' natives over `Number` are declared at `RR64`, and six one-line helpers are added.
- The 16 integer shifts and powers convert in Fortress around bare bindings.
- `SEQV` follows the specification's rule on both paths. `Ratio`, `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` are value objects.
- Walk's loader answers `ilkName` and `SEQV`, and `asString` is `self.ilkName`. The ilk prints `ZZ32`, not `Int`. `match` takes any `String`.
- `Char`'s `asExprString` writes one text on both paths.
- The writer side runs over `JavaBufferedWriter`. `FileWriteStream` stays on glue until the reader rung.
- The code generator compiles `asif`: at a method call, at a call whose dispatched arguments are all assumptions, and as a value.
- Natives on glue went from 143 to 102.
- Rungs S and T never started, for want of disk. I've moved both to climb batch 28, which is on your review list.

input.prompt:
Load the `fortress-repo` skill first, with its parts `references/compiler.md`, `references/worktrees.md`, `references/build-and-caches.md` and `references/session.md`. This is a probe: you read, build and run in a worktree of your own, and edit no tracked file of `/home/user/fortress` (its `main` holds climb batch 27's unpushed landing; change nothing there, and do not build or run in it).

## The question

Climb batch 27's gate (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/distance.txt`, on the merged tree at `151cb4126`, local `main` now at `209192b67`) reads `#total 0`, but no longer `#crash none` as climb batch 26's did (F-54). It holds two crash rows:

- `#crash decl ObjectDecl FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2 IllegalArgumentException Comparison method violates its general contract!` (the declaration is `value object Char`);
- `#crash stage component FortressBuiltin leftover InterpreterBug ** bug! Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes. Component at FortressBuiltin.fss:12.1`.

The post-batch review (`explorations/reviews/batch-27-review.md`, on the local `main`, its finding on the crashes) reads rung C (`wip/rung-char-expr-string`, `2f864ab0b`; worktree `/home/user/fortress-char-expr-string`), which ran neither the count nor the distance stage for want of disk, as the likely cause, by reading only.

Find, with evidence:

1. The crash's cause: the stack trace (the gate's logs: find where the gate stage wrote its distance log, under the main tree's `tmp/` or the gate's output folder named in `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`; read, do not run, there), the comparator that breaks its contract, and which input of `Char`'s declaration feeds it, and which rung's change brought that input (C, or C with another rung's: E made `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` value objects and the code generator marks value objects; A changed walk's loader; F and I moved `Char`-adjacent bindings).
2. Whether it reproduces: run the distance stage (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh`, its header says how) on the merged tree, in a worktree of your own at `a2f0b5cf2` seeded from the base build (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`, base build `/home/user/fortress-base27`) and built as `build-and-caches.md` says; and once on rung C's head if the cause is not plain from the first run. Say whether the crash is deterministic (a contract violation can depend on hash order: run the merged tree twice if the first run's cause is not plain).
3. Whether the crash hides errors: what of `Char`'s body and of the `FortressBuiltin` component's later stages the checker did not check because of it, and, if a one-line local change in your worktree avoids the crash, how many errors the distance then shows there (do not commit the change).
4. The ledger row to file (its text only; do not file it), and the facts made false (F-53, F-54, F-281, F-288 by the review).

Mind the disk: about 5.6G is free; remove your worktree when you are done (its branch, if you made one, need not be pushed or deleted). Write your report to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/REPORT.md`. Your final message, at most 10 lines: the cause, the rung, deterministic or not, what it hides with the count of errors if you measured it, and whether a fix is small.

  - **Where:** in `Char`'s `digit`, the test `x = -1` meets 33 candidates for `=`, and 24 of those are rung N's new pairs.

Your rule says a change to the checker is also made fast, so I'll give it a rung of its own in climb batch 28, with its three sibling sorts. I'll file row 929 for it after the push.

input.prompt:
Load the `fortress-repo` skill first (its committing part included). You change the batch workflow's script and manual, which are the coordinator's tools, not the original tree, so no Fortress test is owed; the script's own check is `explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` (its header says how to run it).

Work in a worktree of your own: `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add -b script/hold-after-repair /home/user/fortress-script-fix main`. Do not edit, commit or push in `/home/user/fortress` (another workflow lands there); commit on your branch by named paths with `fortress-repo`'s footer exactly (plain "Claude", no model name), and do not push. The coordinator lands your commit.

The files: `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`. Read the manual's sections that bear (with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#<heading>'`) and the coordinator skill's `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs", whose rules the script must follow.

## 1. A point that the repair fixed holds no push (the curator's word, 2026-11-07)

In climb batch 27 (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/RECORD.md`, its paragraph "Not pushed"; `JUDGE-review.md`; `REPAIR-review.md`; the run's journal `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/subagents/workflows/wf_72601264-7dd/journal.jsonl`), the merged-diff review returned a point with `holdsPush: true`: a team demo stopped on the merged tree, against P-79. Its judge ruled a repair, the repair fixed walk, all 52 demos reached their end again, and the gate after the repair was green. Yet `pushHeldBy` (`climb-batch-workflow.js`, about line 2084) still held the push, since it reads the review's `pointsReached` with no regard to the repair. The curator: "When it was fixed, then it should land."

Change the script so that a `holdsPush` point that a repair round settled no longer holds the push. The push stays held only by a point that cannot be undone, by a point that still acts against a decision on record after the repairs, or by a gate that stays red after its repair (`batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). Design it so that the script, not an agent's prose, decides: for example, the repair role's schema returns, for each `holdsPush` point it was given, whether its repair settled it, with the evidence, and `pushHeldBy` drops the settled ones; a point marked as one that cannot be undone is never dropped. Keep the change small and in the script's style. Update the manual's text on the hold to match.

## 2. The footer

Commit `b9635f0a7` (the judge's ruling on the merged-diff review) carries a model name in its `Co-Authored-By` line, against `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md`; the agent followed the harness's attribution reminder. The commit stage's footer check (about line 2139) saw it and let it pass. Make every role that commits carry, in its prompt, the exact footer and the line that it overrides any footer that the harness suggests; and make the commit stage's check name such a commit as a defect in its result (it must not rewrite pushed or cited history; a report line that the coordinator routes is enough).

## 3. The disk

The disk allowance ran out during climb batch 27, so rungs S and T never started and other stages skipped their measures (the RECORD's "Not landed" and PLAN's item 68). Add a check at the run's start, before the scatter: read the free space on `/home/user` (`df -P`), and if it is under a floor of about 1.5G per rung plus 4G, stop the run with a clear message before any agent starts, so the coordinator frees disk and launches again. Put the floor's numbers in one constant with a comment of its ground, and state the check in the manual.

Run `workflow-scenarios.js` until it reports 0 problems, and parse the script as its header says. Your final message, at most 10 lines: the commit on your branch, what each of the three changes does, and the scenarios check's result.

content.content:
## Landing its result

The workflow lands its own result, by the curator's rule of 2026-11-03 (`../../HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-11-03)", 06:2x); the design's decision 6, the coordinator's cherry-pick, is reversed. After the judge, the lander, in the main tree:

1. Checks the judge's checks: the branch holds its commits past AT, `mech-final.md` says "Every check passes.", the worktree is clean. If one fails, it lands nothing, and the result's `stopped` says so; the worktree and the branch stay.
2. Puts the commits on `main`: `git merge --ff-only` of the branch when `main` is still at AT, which keeps the judge's hashes; otherwise `git cherry-pick AT..BRANCH`, since `main` moved during the run. A refusal or a conflict is aborted, `main` stays where it was, and the run stops as in step 1.
3. Runs on `main` `record.py check --base <main before the landing>`, `ledger.py landing-check <the batch's base>` and `check-index.sh`. If one fails, `git reset --keep` takes the run's commits off the local `main`, which is not pushed, and the run stops as in step 1.
4. Pushes, in the order of the `fortress-repo` skill's committing part: `git log origin/main..main` lists only the run's commits, then `main`, `main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` and `main:blinded-fable`. A refused push, or another agent's commit in that list, stops the run, landed but not all pushed, before the orientation update.
5. `git worktree remove` the worktree, without `--force`, and `git branch -D` the branch.
6. Reads the facts list of the orientation call in the landed `diff.md`'s "Next" (the entries that the landing and the run added or changed); the script then runs `orientation.js` with `mode: 'update'`, `out` the batch's `climb-batch-N/orientation/` and `stream` `orientation-bN`. Nothing waits on the coordinator between the record's commits and the update. With no entry there, the update is skipped, and the skill update still runs. If the update fails to start, the run stops, landed and pushed, before the skill update. The skill update below installs its result.

Load the `fortress-repo` skill, then read the `coordinator` skill's `references/record.md` whole (`/home/user/fortress/.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`): you are a record worker, and it gives how entries, histories, PLAN and the review queue are written (FACTS and POSITIONS only through `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`). Work in `/home/user/fortress` on `main`; commit by named paths with `fortress-repo`'s footer; do not push (the coordinator pushes). Another agent may commit skill files in this tree meanwhile: on an index.lock error wait five seconds and retry, and leave other uncommitted edits alone.

Four changes:

1. **The curator's decision on question Q1 of `explorations/reviews/natives-remainder-2026-11-07.md`.** His word in chat at 10:5x UTC on 2026-11-07, cleaned: "I don't know how to answer Q1 with the devices for 45 names or for shared carriers. Can you arrange for independent Fable review of this design? I'll take its decision as it lands, and we'll have to review it in detail after it lands." The Fable judgement, worded by an Opus writer with its citations checked, is `explorations/reviews/natives-device-2026-11-07.md`; read its summary and section 3. Its decision: yes to Q1 for all 45 bindings, with three amendments (the arrays' store: the compiled half by P-164's device, walk keeps its own store; threads, `abort` and the task trace: P-167's device over a `nativeHelpers` class over the compiled runtime, `Thread`'s four raising until compiled `spawn`; the numerals: `IntLiteral`'s 8 as Fortress text over `asZZ` before the names batch, the rest at the names batch by P-167's device after a carrier review); it bends P-58's walk half for these names and makes P-167's table of two names a rule. Write it into POSITIONS as his decision, in the form `record.md` gives (a new entry, or P-167 widened, whichever `record.md` and the entries' shape call for), with its history naming his word and the judgement as the ground, and the bend of P-58 stated in P-58 or its history as `record.md` says. Do not record the judgement's reframed Q2 as decided: it is a question still open for him (the store's shape: a cell per element, the default, or a slot API in the compiled transaction).
2. **A review-queue item** for his detailed review of that decision, as he asked, in `explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md`'s form, under the theme that fits, pointing at the entry and the review.
3. **PLAN's line on `NativeArray`.** PLAN (`explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`) says that D2's `NativeArray` waits for array decision A after the switch-over. The natives review's main finding (its section on `NativeArray`, and the summary) shows that this does not hold: every array, vector, varargs list and `args` of the one library is built on `PrimitiveArray`, so a compiled program would fail at its first array without a compiled store before the switch-over. Correct that line, with the review as its ground; move the old words to PLAN-history if `record.md` asks for it.
4. **The footer item.** The record-landing workflow filed the post-batch review's finding B (the model name in commit `b9635f0a7`'s footer) as an item for the curator. His word in chat at 14:19 UTC on 2026-11-07: he does not care about a model name in a commit's footer and wants no report of it. Remove that item, and any PLAN line or review-list line that reports it, leaving at most a line in the item's history if `record.md` wants one. Search with `grep -n -i -E 'b9635f0a7|footer|model name' explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`.

Run `record.py check`, `ledger.py check` and `explorations/coordinator/check-index.sh` before your commit. Your final message, at most 10 lines: the entry written (its number and title), the queue item's number, the PLAN line's old and new words, what was removed for the footer, and the commit.

content.content:
## Preparing a batch record

An Opus planning worker drafts `CLIMB-BATCH-<n>.md`. A Fable reviewer edits it in place with one reason per change. The coordinator reads the diff and brings the record's questions to the curator one per message. The batch launches on the answers or on the standing go (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The go").

The planner builds each rung's briefing as in-context learning: the agents were not trained on Fortress, and the language was never finished (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). A briefing holds what the rung's section cites: the decisions and earlier rulings it rests on, its ledger rows, the specification's sections whole by their headings, the notes on the subject by section, and the library code that is the precedent. Process positions and harness facts stay out, because the brief's role text and the skill carry them. In batch 10 the workers named none of the 87 POSITIONS and FACTS keys before their fix edits (`process-engineering/context-study.md`, section 5). Each key goes through `facts-extract.sh --check` on the base, every key matching exactly one place. Each carries one line on why it is there. The planner marks the `checks` sub-list: the decisions and rows the checks need, and the sections and precedent code they compare against.

A rung that changes what an implementation does is briefed with the Appendix I Effects and the specification's notes that its change makes false, found by a grep while the record is prepared. Batch 9's record gave rung K none, and Appendix I's `comprises` Effect was that batch's one blocking finding (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, finding 3).

A record asks a rung for no corpus-wide output comparison, no ladder before-run, no microGPT check and no specification build log (P-103, "The suite's verdict is the check."; the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "What a brief holds"). Whole suites are the skill's rule (`tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). A count of the programs a change reaches, when a decision needs one, is the planner's probe, taken before the record is written. A named one-time count of changed outputs is asked only where a decision of the curator's names it for that rung. The coordinator starts its base pass before the launch (`tools/count-run/count-run.sh`).

A ledger note that the record briefs fits its row: the planner reads the row with `ledger.py show N` against the tool's limits (notes 700 characters, the row 1,200) and, where the note does not fit, briefs the row's whole new line. Climb batch 26's record briefed rung S a note to row 440, whose notes held 676 of 700 characters (`reviews/batch-26-review.md`, process finding 6).

The record's section on how it is run gives the manifest's fields rung by rung, the intro every agent reads, and the launch steps. It holds no copy of the block: the batch's generator writes the block from the record.

## Before the launch

The coordinator, in this order:

1. The script, this manual and the batch's manifest generator on `main`. The base is `main`'s head after them, by its full hash, passed as `args.base`.
2. The batch's one base build, a worktree at the base outside the main tree, built once and then left alone. Every rung worktree is seeded from it, and the old code runs from it (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). About 200 s, as the skill's `worktrees.md`, "Finding or building a base build", gives it:

        git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add --detach /home/user/fortress-base<N> <base>
        cd /home/user/fortress-base<N>      # then set up the call as the skill's build-and-caches.md says
        ant compileAll                      # BUILD SUCCESSFUL
        # the library order (build-and-caches.md, "The library order"), then one walk run, which warms walk's caches:
        bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
        git status --porcelain              # empty: the seed refuses a base build that is not clean

   Its path goes to the launch as `args.baseBuild`. The script refuses to start without it (scenario B1).
3. One trial seed proves the base build, about 3 s: `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck - <base>`, then `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-seedcheck`. One `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck-caches ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, run from the main tree, proves the old code runs; its folder is removed after.
4. The briefings checked on the base (`python3 explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/manifest/lists<N>.py`). The block generated (`gen<N>.py`), checked in a scratch copy and spliced (`check<N>.js`, then `check<N>.js --write`). Then `node explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` on the spliced script, which also checks that every skill section the script cites by name is a heading of the skill. Then the commit.
5. `df -P /home/user`, its Available column at or above the script's floor, 1.5 G a rung plus 4 G ("The disk before the scatter"), which the script reads again before the scatter and stops under. `git status --porcelain` empty in the main tree, and no other agent writing there or pushing `main` while the run gathers and commits. The session's permission rules let the commit stage run `tools/mg-run.sh`.
6. Check-ins armed for the run's length, 45 minutes apart (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "Watching a run").

The launch: `Workflow({scriptPath: 'explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js', args: {base: '<full hash>', baseBuild: '/home/user/fortress-base<N>'}})`. The args are kept byte for byte, since a resume needs them. The base build stays until the coordinator removes it after the landing.

input.description: Plan climb batch 28
input.prompt:
Load the `fortress-repo` skill first, read its `references/revival-changes.md` whole, and the parts your probes need. You are the planner of climb batch 28 of the Fortress revival, phase 4's sixth batch: you write its batch record, `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md`, and run the probes it needs. Read the batch manual's "Preparing a batch record" and "Before the launch" (`explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#Preparing a batch record'`), and the `coordinator` skill's `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/batch.md`, "The go" and "The workflow", whose rules bind the record. Take `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-27.md` as the form (its sections: the manifest rung by rung, the points for the curator, the forks with their defaults, the rungs, the candidates and probes, how it is run, the files cited); copy its form, not its content.

## The mission

The goal of this phase is the switch-over, the compiled path moved onto the interpreter's library, and its first step is the natives: every `builtinPrimitive` binding of that library made to run on the compiled path (P-33, P-37, P-58). After climb batch 27, 341 of 443 live bindings name a helper and 102 a glue class (F-32, F-299). The decisions on record wish this batch to move the project as far toward zero as the work that is well defined allows: run the probes needed to decide how the remaining natives are solved, then plan every piece that they make well defined. A batch takes every piece of work on PLAN's road that is well defined (its decisions taken), conflicts with nothing and moves the project forward; a piece waits only where it would put the merge at risk (`batch.md`, "The go").

## The candidates (each with its ground; verify each against the tree at `main`)

content.content:
The judge judged three sections "install" and none "hold". I checked with `diff` that `orientation.md` differs from the old part only in those three sections, so I copied it whole. `revival-changes.md` grew from 20,192 to 22,974 characters. The judge accepted the size overrun.

- **Dispatch and overloading.** The old text did not warn about this. A program's trait with its own functional `+` must exclude `Number` or arrays, or walk refuses the program at load. The same holds for `-`, `MIN` and `MAX`.
- **Traits and objects.**
  - The old text did not say what `=` does when a type declares none. It now says that `=` is then `SEQV`: a value object compares field by field, and a string only to itself.
  - It also says where to write the `I extends Index` bound until the switch-over.
- **Numbers.**
  - The old text gave an example that walk now prints differently. It now says that walk prints `Cell[\ZZ32\]` for a value that is a `Cell[\Int\]`.
  - New rule: `Number` declares nothing. Generic code over `T extends Number` can call nothing on a `T`.
  - New rule: two numbers of different types are `=` only through a coercion. Otherwise the answer is `false`.

The new `sources.md` section, "Climb batch 27's update", holds the provenance.

## Sentences changed
